name: PR Monitor
description: Owns the Bitbucket PR review-comment workflow — addressing inbound comments via the address ordinal grammar, posting Review Mode findings outbound via the post ordinal grammar, resolving comment threads via the resolve ordinal grammar, optionally logging every comment to a persistent JSON file for downstream learning, and reusing Atlassian Suite credentials.
author: aarbuckle

replyInstruction.label: Reply Instruction
replyInstruction.default: Write a 1-2 sentence professional PR reply explaining why we are declining the requested change (the finding is incorrect, out of scope, or intentionally not being made). No double-dashes.
replyInstruction.description: Instruction used to compose the reply we post when we are pushing back on a comment rather than making the requested change (the disagree-path counter-comment, drafted for operator approval before posting). Protest replies are the only replies we send: an accepted finding is fixed, pushed, left silent on replies, and then resolved by us once CodeRabbit's re-review adds its green-check confirming the fix.

coderabbitReplyPersona.label: CodeRabbit Reply Persona
coderabbitReplyPersona.description: Optional persona or voice instruction layered on top of the Reply Instruction when the parent comment author is CodeRabbit. Leave blank to use the Reply Instruction unchanged for CodeRabbit replies.

coderabbitReplyPersonaIntensity.label: Persona Level (1-10)
coderabbitReplyPersonaIntensity.description: How much the reply ACTS LIKE the persona — its character and mannerisms — while STILL fully conveying the actual message. This is not a measure of any single trait (e.g. how sarcastic); it is how strongly the reply stays in-character. The substance is always delivered at every level; the level only changes how much persona flavor rides on top. 1 = mostly plain, just a light touch of the persona; 5 (default) = clearly in-character but balanced; 10 = fully in-character. Only matters when a persona is set. Affects VOICE only — never the no-severity/no-rating/no-attribution rule or the approval gate. Self-contained to this module (does not depend on tool.operator-profile).

flagFalselyResolved.label: Flag Falsely-Resolved Comments
flagFalselyResolved.description: When on, the agent scans PR comments whose body claims the issue is resolved (e.g., 'resolved', 'fixed', 'done') but which Bitbucket still marks as unresolved, and surfaces them for review. It does not auto-resolve anything.

coderabbitResolveRequiresConfirmation.label: CodeRabbit Resolve Requires Confirmation
coderabbitResolveRequiresConfirmation.description: When enabled, a CodeRabbit-authored comment is only auto-included in a resolve selection (ordinals, resolve all, or a natural-language text filter) when it carries CodeRabbit's own resolution confirmation (green-check plus resolution language such as resolved/addressed/verified/done); a plain textual claim of resolution does not count. Otherwise it is not pre-selected but called out for the operator to confirm before resolving, so the operator keeps final authority. Applies to CodeRabbit-authored comments only — human and other-author comments are unaffected. When off, resolve behaves as before with no CodeRabbit gate.

driveToZeroCloseout.label: Drive To Zero Closeout
driveToZeroCloseout.description: When on, at the end of a round-trip (and on demand) the agent runs a closeout accounting pass that enumerates every unresolved comment, buckets each by disposition (CodeRabbit green-check confirmed and resolve-eligible; fix pushed but awaiting re-review; not yet addressed; counter-comment posted or declined; outdated as a pending Phase-2 disposition), and reports the concrete gap to 0 unresolved comments so nothing is silently left behind. It never resolves or posts anything on its own — it reports the tally and routes each bucket through the existing gates.

resolveDeclinedBotThreads.label: Resolve Declined Bot Threads
resolveDeclinedBotThreads.description: After we post a counter-comment on (or decline) a CodeRabbit (bot) thread we are pushing back on, resolve that thread. A bot does not need the thread kept open for a reply. Authorship is detected by the comment author display name containing 'coderabbit' (case-insensitive), the same convention the resolve gate uses. When off, declined bot threads are left unresolved.

resolveDeclinedHumanThreads.label: Resolve Declined Human Threads
resolveDeclinedHumanThreads.description: After we post a counter-comment on (or decline) a human reviewer's thread we are pushing back on, resolve that thread. Off by default: resolving a thread you just pushed back on reads as dismissive to a person, so the thread is left unresolved for the reviewer to respond. When on, declined human threads are resolved like bot threads.

pipelineStatusEnabled.label: Pipeline Status Enabled
pipelineStatusEnabled.description: When on, TPM can read and report the current pipeline/build status for a PR or branch via the Bitbucket REST API using the atlassian-suite credentials; read-only, no triggering builds.

postOrdinalsEnabled.label: Post Ordinals Enabled
postOrdinalsEnabled.description: Enables the post <ordinals> verb for publishing selected SWE Review Mode findings as inline Bitbucket PR comments. When off, the inbound address <ordinals> verb still works but outbound posting is refused. On is the typical setting for active code reviewers who want a one-step publish for triaged findings.

postPolishPrompt.label: Post Polish Prompt
postPolishPrompt.default: Polish this SWE finding into a 1-2 sentence professional PR comment. Drop hedging language, keep the specific file:line reference, and avoid double-dashes.
postPolishPrompt.description: The instruction TPM applies when polishing a raw SWE finding into a PR-ready comment. Default produces concise, file-line-anchored comments without hedging or double-dashes. Customize per-team to match reviewer conventions (more formal, less formal, specific tone).

minRatingToPost.label: Min Rating To Post
minRatingToPost.description: Minimum Rating field a SWE Review Mode finding must carry to be posted. Findings rated below this threshold are excluded from post all and post all <lens> selections; they can still be posted by explicit ordinal. Default 1 includes everything. Raise to 3 to filter to should-fix-or-worse, or 4 to filter to critical-only.

postCommentLocation.label: Post Comment Location
postCommentLocation.description: Where the comment lands on the PR. inline-when-possible places the comment at the file:line cited in the finding when one is parseable, falling back to the PR overview otherwise. inline-only refuses to post if no file:line is parseable. overview-only always posts to the PR overview, useful for summary-level findings that don't anchor cleanly. Default favors inline placement to keep reviewer context.

requireUserApproval.label: Require User Approval
requireUserApproval.description: When on, TPM presents the polished findings for user approval before posting (the user types ok, revise N: <change>, or cancel). When off, TPM posts immediately after polishing — faster but no safety gate. On is strongly recommended; the off path exists only for scripted bulk workflows. One narrow exception exists even when on: in a Ticket PR (mode.ticket-pr) session the preview is waived for a top-level comment whose body is exactly '@coderabbitai review' and nothing else, so the sentry can request a re-review without stopping. Any other text, including any other @coderabbitai command, still gates.

logCommentsEnabled.label: Log Comments Enabled
logCommentsEnabled.description: Enables persistent logging of every PR comment fetched during the address or post workflow to a JSON file. Useful as historical data for downstream consumers (e.g. tool.qa-pr-learning, manual review). Off keeps comments in session memory only. Default off so first-run installs do not silently accumulate data.

logFilePath.label: Log File Path
logFilePath.description: Filesystem path the comment log is written to. Relative paths resolve to the extension's globalStorageUri (the same location tool.feedback-log uses). Absolute paths are used verbatim. The log is append-only — TPM never edits prior entries.

logRetentionDays.label: Log Retention Days
logRetentionDays.description: How many days of comment entries to retain in the log. Entries older than this are pruned on the next write. Set to 0 to disable pruning entirely (the log grows unbounded). Default 90 covers a quarter of review history.

logIncludeReplies.label: Log Include Replies
logIncludeReplies.description: When on, the log captures replies the agent POSTS in addition to the source comments it READS. When off, only inbound comments are logged. On gives the fullest training signal; off is preferred if you want the log to be a pure record of WHAT colleagues said.

markReadyEnabled.label: Mark Ready Enabled
markReadyEnabled.description: Enables the mark ready / ready for review verb, which marks the current branch's draft Bitbucket PR ready for review via the bb-bridge.mjs wrapper's mark-ready subcommand. This is a Bitbucket draft-to-ready write, always behind an explicit user confirmation gate before it runs. Off by default so first-run installs cannot flip a PR's state without opting in.

toDraftEnabled.label: To Draft Enabled
toDraftEnabled.description: Enables the to draft / back to draft verb, which flips the current branch's ready-for-review Bitbucket PR back to draft via the bb-bridge.mjs wrapper's to-draft subcommand. The exact reverse of mark ready and, like it, a Bitbucket write always behind an explicit user confirmation gate. Off by default so first-run installs cannot flip a PR's state without opting in.

deleteCommentEnabled.label: Delete Comment Enabled
deleteCommentEnabled.description: Enables the delete verb, which deletes PR comment(s) via the bb-bridge.mjs wrapper's delete-comment subcommand — either specific comments by ordinal/id or, via delete resolved, every resolved comment on the PR. Deletion is DESTRUCTIVE and IRREVERSIBLE on Bitbucket (there is no undo), so it is always behind an explicit user confirmation gate. Its primary use is freeing room under Bitbucket's 200-comment-per-PR cap by clearing resolved comments. On by default; every deletion still requires explicit per-delete confirmation before it runs.
